title: Hudhud: The Atlas of Wonders
subtitle: The light workshop
review_note: This is a game, not a history. The Atlas of Stories, its scattered pages, this workshop and every word spoken in it are invented for play. Ibn al-Haytham was a real scholar, and what the museum knows of him is one link away. Historical review pending: the museum records linked here have not yet been through historical review for this game.
art_note: The pictures in this scene are drawn by code that an AI agent wrote. They follow pictures the museum's founder supplied, and are a trial of the look, not finished art.
start_hint: Fly with the arrow keys and Space. Press E to touch things. Everything can also be done from the list under the picture.
canvas_label: The workshop, as a picture. The list after it says the same in words.
objective_light: Turn the mirrors until the light reaches the pale page.
objective_done: The page has its ink back. Go to it when you are ready to finish.
hint_story: The glowing mirrors still need a turn.
d_intro_1: There! A page of the Atlas blew in here. Its ink has gone pale.
d_intro_2: Pale ink needs light. But this room is kept dark.
d_intro_3: One thin beam comes in by the shutter. Let us turn the mirrors and send it to the page!
d_scholar_1: Welcome, small travellers. I am testing how light moves.
d_scholar_2: It runs straight until something turns it or stops it. Try my mirrors and see.
c_thanks: Thank you. We will try the mirrors.
d_scholar_dark_1: In a dark room, one thin beam is easy to follow. You can stop it with your hand, or measure it with a ruler.
d_scholar_dark_2: So the dark is not for hiding. It is for seeing better!
d_scholar_see_1: Some old books say that sight leaps out of the eye. I hold that light comes from the thing to the eye.
d_scholar_see_2: So when I look at you, your light is visiting me.
d_scholar_bye: Test it yourselves. That is the best way to know.
d_scholar_after: A straight beam, turned five times. You did not take my word for it: you tried.
d_cat_1: Hello, whiskers. I am a bird, but a friendly one.
d_cat_3: She has found the warmest spot in the room.
d_page_dark: The ink is too pale to read. It needs the beam.
d_solved_1: Look! The ink is coming back!
d_solved_2: Straight lines, turned by mirrors. Now you have seen it for yourselves.
d_solved_3: One page ready to go home to the Atlas. Come to it when you are ready.
d_secret_1: The rooftops! They are on the wall, and they are upside down!
d_secret_2: A small hole and a dark room: the outside draws itself inside, turned over.
d_secret_3: A picture made of nothing but light.
d_feather_1: One of my feathers! The storm must have carried it out here.
beam_end_block: It stops at the tower of books.
beam_end_loop: It goes round in a ring.
cap_restored: A bright chime: the ink returns.
goal_curiosity_how: Ask for more, or find what the dark room hides.
goal_ingenuity_how: Light the page in {n} turns or fewer.
goal_kindness_how: Stop to greet the workshop cat.
note_1: Ibn al-Haytham was born in Basra around the year 965 and later lived in Cairo. His best-known book is on optics: light and sight.
note_2: The museum's record says he let light into a dark room through a small hole, to test that it travels in straight lines and that a solid body cuts it.
note_3: The same record says he held that light goes from the thing to the eye.
note_uncertain: Not from the records: this workshop, its cat, the mirrors on stands and the glass prism are invented for the game. The pictures this scene follows show a prism; no museum record read for the scene says he used one.
style_story_how: More flaps, a slower glide, and the mirrors that need a turn glow.
style_explorer_how: The game as it is meant.
style_challenge_how: Every mirror starts wrong, and Ingenuity allows no spare turn.
